modelIntro.title: What Is Wan 2.7 AI Video Generator?
description: Wan 2.7 is Alibaba's video generation model family for text-to-video, image-to-video, and reference-to-video creation. It is built for short clips that need stronger prompt following, reference-guided subjects, multi-shot structure, camera direction, and synchronized audio cues.

Use Wan 2.7 when a single prompt needs to describe the scene, reference media, shot order, first and last frames, continuation timing, motion style, lighting, and sound. It fits product ads, ASMR material clips, social videos, storyboard tests, character motion, and reference-led commercial drafts.

promptExamples.title: Wan 2.7 Prompt Examples
promptExamples.subtitle: Copy these examples when you need multi-shot motion, reference control, first/last-frame transitions, or synchronized sound.

items.title: Multi-Shot Product Launch
items.prompt: Create a Wan 2.7 video for a matte black wireless speaker. Shot 1: slow push-in on the speaker on a concrete table. Shot 2: close-up of the fabric grille vibrating with bass. Shot 3: water droplets slide across the surface. Shot 4: the speaker sits in a warm living room at sunset. Keep the product shape consistent, add soft camera motion, clean reflections, deep bass pulses, and subtle room ambience.
items.description: Uses a clear shot order, product consistency, camera movement, material detail, and audio timing.

items.title: First and Last Frame Transition
items.prompt: Animate from the uploaded first frame of a closed sketchbook on a desk to the uploaded last frame of the same sketchbook open with a finished city map. The camera stays top-down, pages turn naturally, pencil lines draw themselves across the paper, desk objects remain fixed, and the final map lands exactly on the last reference frame with soft paper rustle.
items.description: Shows how to write a controlled first-and-last-frame transition without changing the scene layout.

items.title: Reference-to-Video Character Scene
items.prompt: Use three references: a character design sheet, a rainy alley background, and a short neon sign video. Create a Wan 2.7 clip where the character walks toward the camera, stops under the sign, and looks up as rain reflects on the coat. Preserve the face, outfit, colors, and alley layout. Add slow side-tracking camera movement, footsteps, rain on metal, and a low city hum.
items.description: Assigns a clear job to each reference so identity, background, motion, and sound stay organized.

items.title: Continuation With Native Sound
items.prompt: Continue the uploaded cafe counter video. Keep the same framing, lighting, cup position, and barista hands. The milk stream starts thin, becomes a smooth spiral, and finishes as a leaf pattern on the latte. Add synchronized pouring sound, ceramic cup contact, quiet machine hum, and no sudden camera jump.
items.description: Uses video continuation language, stable framing, precise motion timing, and synchronized audio cues.

troubleshooting.title: Prompt Tips for Better Wan 2.7 Results
troubleshooting.subtitle: Stronger Wan 2.7 prompts tell the model what changes, what stays fixed, and how the camera and sound should move over time.

items.title: Turn a broad idea into a shot order
items.desc: Weak prompt: A cool sneaker commercial. Better prompt:
items.prompt: Create a sneaker commercial. Shot 1: macro close-up of the sole touching wet pavement. Shot 2: side tracking shot as the runner accelerates. Shot 3: slow push-in on the shoe logo under neon reflections. Keep the same sneaker design, add splash sound, city ambience, and crisp lighting.

items.title: Give every reference a role
items.desc: Weak prompt: Use these images and make a video. Better prompt:
items.prompt: Use image 1 for the character face and outfit, image 2 for the room layout, and video 1 for the neon light motion. Create a clip where the character turns toward the window while the neon reflection moves across the wall. Preserve identity, clothing colors, and room geometry.

items.title: Write sound as timed action
items.desc: Weak prompt: Make ASMR with good audio. Better prompt:
items.prompt: Create a macro ASMR clip of a glass fruit being sliced. The blade enters early, the fruit cracks midway, and tiny pieces slide apart before the ending. Add crisp glass tapping, soft cutting pressure, quiet table contact, and no background music.

faq.q: What is Wan 2.7 AI Video Generator?
faq.a: Wan 2.7 is Alibaba's video generation model family for creating short videos from text, images, video references, and audio direction. On Toolaze, it is presented as a browser-based Wan 2.7 generator with prompt, output, and reference controls.

faq.q: What creation modes does Wan 2.7 support?
faq.a: Wan 2.7 supports text-to-video, image-to-video, and reference-to-video. Reference-to-video can use image, video, and audio references to guide the subject, scene, motion, and sound.

Yes. Wan 2.7 can use image references, including first-frame and first-and-last-frame style control. For reference-to-video, Wan 2.7 supports up to five total image or video references in supported modes.
Yes. Wan 2.7 reference-to-video can use video references, and Wan 2.7 image-to-video includes video continuation so a source clip can continue with matching framing, lighting, and motion direction.
Yes. Wan 2.7 supports audio-video synchronization for effects, ambience, music, and voice-style direction. For best results, write sound as timed scene action instead of adding a vague audio request.
Yes. Wan 2.7 supports multi-shot prompting. Write the sequence as Shot 1, Shot 2, and Shot 3, then describe what changes and what should remain consistent across the clip.

faq.q: What duration and resolution can Wan 2.7 create?
faq.a: Wan 2.7 supports a 2 to 15 second duration range with 720p or 1080p output. Toolaze shows the available duration and resolution choices in the generator before you create the video.

faq.q: How should I write a Wan 2.7 prompt?
faq.a: Include the subject, reference roles, motion, camera movement, shot order, timing, lighting, and sound. Short, structured prompts usually work better than broad cinematic descriptions.

faq.q: How many Toolaze Credits does Wan 2.7 cost?
faq.a: Wan 2.7 starts at 64 Credits for a 720p, 2-second generation on Toolaze. Longer duration or 1080p output increases the required Credits before generation.
Wan 2.7 video generation depends on your available Credits, account state, selected duration, and selected resolution. The generator shows the current Credits requirement before generation.

faq.q: When should I choose Wan 2.7 instead of Wan 2.6 or Wan 2.5?
faq.a: Choose Wan 2.7 when you need the newest Wan controls, richer references, first/last-frame transitions, video continuation, multi-shot prompts, and synchronized sound. Choose Wan 2.6 or Wan 2.5 for simpler Wan clips with fewer setup choices.

faq.q: When should I choose another Toolaze video model?
faq.a: Choose Kling when high-resolution action or dramatic motion is the priority, Seedance when director-style scene planning is more important, and Grok Imagine Video when you want a faster draft from an image.
